citeAs: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym. Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267.
creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang (UC Berkeley, UIUC, CMU, Apple)
description: SWE-Gym is the first training environment for software engineering agents, containing 2,438 real-world task instances sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories. Each instance comprises a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language. It is designed to train language model based SWE agents and verifiers, combining real-world GitHub issues with pre-installed dependencies and executable test verification.
name: SWE-Gym
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations involved manually configuring dependencies for each task instance using relevant configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt), CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot at the time of issue creation. Execution-based validation was used to verify that gold patches pass more unit tests than the original code. The process required approximately 200 human annotation hours.
rai:dataBiases: The task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern, with pandas comprising nearly one-third of the total tasks and bokeh representing only one percent. Tasks in SWE-Gym are on average harder than those in SWE-Bench. The dataset is limited to Python repositories and 11 specific open-source projects. Repeated sampling introduces a bias toward easier tasks (long-tail success distribution), which the authors address with per-instance capping. Manual environment configuration may bias the dataset away from tasks with complex dependencies.
rai:dataCollection: SWE-Gym was constructed by first using SEART GitHub search to filter repositories (created before July 1, 2022, with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests and 100 contributors), yielding 358 repositories. SWE-Bench's instance extraction script was used to convert repositories into task instances. Executable environments were manually configured using relevant configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation. SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script was used to ensure gold patches pass more unit tests than the original code. The process required approximately 200 human annotation hours and 10,000 CPU core hours.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of Python GitHub issues (pull requests) including natural language descriptions of issues, repository snapshots, and solution code diffs. SWE-Gym Raw contains 64,689 task instances spanning 358 Python repositories, extracted without executable environments.
rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories (11), types of tasks, and programming languages (Python only). The dataset is limited to 2,438 instances, and performance is currently limited by the compute budget for sampling rather than the number of tasks. The dataset focuses on repository-level Python tasks from GitHub and may not generalize to other programming languages or task types.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: SWE-Gym Lite was created as a subset of 230 tasks by following the SWE-Bench Lite filtering pipeline, excluding tasks that require editing more than one file, tasks with poorly described problem statements, those with excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Instances were extracted using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script. Version numbers were associated with instances and environments set up version-by-version. Dependencies were manually configured for each task instance using configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt), CI scripts, or documentation. SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script was used to ensure gold patches pass more unit tests than the original code. Failed instances were filtered out, resulting in 2,438 validated instances. Pre-built Docker images were created for each instance.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility across industries. The agents may impact software engineering jobs and require careful consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code.
rai:dataUseCases: Training language model based software engineering agents via rejection sampling fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Training verifier (reward) models for inference-time scaling. Evaluating SWE agent performance. Enabling scalable learning for software engineering agents to automatically resolve GitHub issues.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEART GitHub search was used to filter repositories. SWE-Bench's instance extraction script was used to convert repositories into task instances. SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script was used to verify instances. The Qwen-2.5-Coder-Instruct-7B tokenizer was used to estimate the number of tokens in trajectories.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a number of independent annotations per item; environment setup was done once per instance.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or annotation quality analysis are discussed in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No specific annotation platform (e.g., MTurk, Label Studio) is mentioned; annotations were done by the authors themselves.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling beyond filtering out failed instances during validation.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No data imputation protocol is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described for the dataset.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of GitHub issues and code repositories; no personal or sensitive information is discussed.
null_reasons.publisher: The evidence quote ('we open source all artifacts') does not name a specific publishing organization; the HuggingFace org name 'SWE-Gym' is inferred from the HF dataset page, not stated in the paper itself. The paper only lists author institutions, not a named publisher entity.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper only says 'Annotations are done by a subset of the authors' — no demographic details (nationality, language, expertise level) are provided beyond this minimal statement.

evidence.rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym, while effective, is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages. We also experiment with inference-time scaling through verifiers trained on agent trajectories sampled from SWE-Gym.
